title: Concrete element-site fibre, set restriction and direct-sum constructions
statement: Let $C$ be a small category with Grothendieck topology $J$, and let $A$ be a sheaf of sets, all in the common universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the element projection $p_A$, topology $J_A$ and restricted ring $R_A$ of [def-sfb-element-site-localization]. For $U\in C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $s\in A(U)$, write $\operatorname{elementObj}(A,U,s)$ for the corresponding object in the opposite of the element site. For an object $(F\xrightarrow{q}A)$ of the sheaf slice, define its fibre family by $(U,s)\mapsto\{x\in F(U):q_U(x)=s\}$. Give this family the restrictions inherited from $F$; on a map $f:(F\to A)\to(G\to A)$ send $(x,q_U(x)=s)$ to $(f_U(x),q'_U(f_U(x))=s)$. This defines the fibre presheaf functor from the sheaf slice to presheaves on the element site. Define the set-sheaf restriction $j_A^{-1}$ by precomposition with $p_A^{\mathrm{op}}$, so $(j_A^{-1}H)(U,s)=H(U)$, with all restrictions and maps inherited from $H$. For a ring sheaf $R$ and an $R_A$-module sheaf $L$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], define the direct-sum presheaf of $R$-modules by $U\mapsto\bigoplus_{s\in A(U)}L(U,s)$. Its restriction along $v:V\to U$ sends the summand indexed by $s$ to the summand indexed by $A(v)(s)$ through the restriction of $L$ along the corresponding element arrow; its scalar action is the $R(U)$-action on each summand.
